newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Aide to EU's Kinnock says no slot decision yet.
newsitem.headline: Aide to EU's Kinnock says no slot decision yet.

text.p: The European Commission is not yet ready for a decision on how to revamp rules governing the allocation of take-off and landing slots at European Union airports, a senior official said on Thursday.
"The Commission has not finished its discussions on this," Philipe Lowe, chief aide to European Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock, told a news conference.

"The Commission has been looking at this...because it believes that the present application rules are unsatisfactory. Our major concern is to ensure that existing rules provide for sufficient new entrants," he added.

Kinnock and the Commission's transport officials had intended last year to propose revised rules allowing some form of trading to replace the so-called "grey market" in peak-period slots which is acknowledged to exist now.

Their plans ran into trouble with European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert, who strongly opposes slot sales on the grounds that they could reinforce the positions of airlines which already dominate their home airports.

The issue spilled over into the British and Commission competition inquiries into the planned alliance between British Airways and AMR Corporation's American Airlines, clearance of which is likely to include the airlines giving up slots at London's Heathrow.
"The existing regulation doesn't provide for secondary trading in slots, it allows for their exchange. In practice, it's not clear that monetary exchanges do not go on," Lowe said.
Lowe added that if trading were allowed there would be a "major concern about those financially strong and powerful airlines at those airports which are particularly congested".
